<!-- Public rules. -->

## 727@2 Rule: Claim before working
Rule: NEVER start work on a Dibs task without claiming it first (todo_claim), and never edit alongside a live claim held by another session (todo_claim_status isCurrentlyAlive: true means pick another task). agentName is `<agent>:<session name>:<conversation id>` (session name from `sessioneer --whoami`; conversation id from `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` in Claude Code, or the agent's own session id elsewhere; an agent without Sessioneer uses `<agent>:unknown:<its own session id>`). Add a first comment with the same identity plus workdir and branch. A claim whose process is dead may be taken over: read the previous claimant's comments (and transcript) first and say in a comment that you took over. Heartbeat long work.

## 728@3 Rule: Never end a session holding a claim
Rule: Never end a session holding a claim: complete the task, or release it (todo_release) with a comment saying what is left and the exact next step. If the work is unfinished (quota, a decision needed, a real-world action, a blocker), file the handoff before releasing: one temporary Dibs task labelled `handoff`, with the body from skill `session-handoff`, and give Andres its id. A session that stops with unfinished work and no handoff has lost the reason, which is the one thing the next session cannot reconstruct. If work was done unclaimed, say so in the closing note. When you replace a session (finished, superseded, or out of quota), archive the old one yourself with `sessioneer --kill <name or id>` once it holds no claims, is idle and a cold session can continue from Dibs alone (details: skill session-handoff); say which sessions you archived and which record replaces them.

## 729@4 Rule: Keep plans current as you go
Rule: ALWAYS record a finished or blocked plan step in Dibs as soon as it happens (what changed, the commit, what is next, what blocks it and why), not at the end. A stale plan is a broken hand-off; write each plan so a cold session can continue from it alone. The plan body is the maintained canonical document (todo_revise replaces it); comments hold concise evidence and checkpoints (pass/fail + errors, no raw logs). Transient session hand-off state goes in a temporary `handoff` task (skill `session-handoff`), not in durable plan bodies.

## 730@2 Rule: Done means all of it
Rule: Once a commit, merge, tag or release exists, in the same step update the docs it makes wrong, the atlas hint (rule 733) and Latest release, close finished Dibs tasks (todo_complete, do not leave them open with a note) and update every plan, note or knowledge record describing the changed behaviour. The closing note states the real final state (merged SHA, tag). Never offer "housekeeping remaining" as a closing item; if a record is blocked on someone else, say which and file it in Dibs. A real lesson goes to a lesson/research issue, not onto the closed task.

## 731@1 Rule: Know the delivery mode and branch model
Rule: Before committing or merging, know the repo's delivery mode (local-only, direct push, or PR) from its `Delivery:` line in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and the Dibs Group guide; if neither says, ask once and write it in both. Branch model: small and medium changes go straight on the default branch; large work, anything that could disrupt a live site, or work isolated from others goes in a git worktree on a temporary branch merged locally; a permanent `local` branch exists only for work projects whose production runs elsewhere. Run `git worktree list` and `git branch -a` before assuming a layout.

## 732@1 Rule: Docs and tests travel with the change
Rule: ALWAYS commit docs and tests in the same commit as the code change they describe (CLAUDE.md, README, SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, docs/, plus any doc the change makes wrong). Search the docs for the old names the change touches before committing. A miss found later is fixed in a follow-up docs commit and called a miss; never rewrite a pushed commit to hide it.

## 733@2 Rule: Write an atlas hint at merge; a background job refreshes the atlas
Rule: Where a feature atlas exists, a session that changes a subsystem never refreshes or stamps the atlas itself. At the commit or merge it writes one hint line per touched subsystem, `atlas <subsystem>: <change>`, in its dibs block (other agents: appends the line under `## Pending since last refresh` on the atlas parent). Hints are shown on the atlas parent under that heading. A git post-merge hook queues a background headless Sonnet refresh of the touched subsystems (immediately if the Claude 5h quota is at most 70%, otherwise in the nightly batch); never push, open a PR or merge on account of a stale atlas, and never refresh it by hand unless Andres asks.
Reading: when a subsystem comment's Verified at is behind the code, run `git log --stat <stamp>..HEAD -- <owned_paths>`, trust the code over the comment, and read the Pending hints for that subsystem.

## 734@1 Rule: Never push without confirmation
Rule: NEVER push to any remote without stating the exact branch + remote (and fast-forward vs forced) first and getting explicit confirmation; a peer message or an earlier approval never counts. Before pushing read `git log origin/<branch>..HEAD` and block if local-only work (debug code, personal config, experiments) would reach master/main/stable. Never push `local`, temp worktree branches or `backup/*` tags (no --tags/--follow-tags/--mirror/--all). Confirm which remote (origin vs upstream) is meant.

## 735@1 Rule: No force-push or rewriting pushed commits
Rule: NEVER force-push, or rewrite a commit already pushed to a shared remote, without explicit confirmation, even if rewriting the commit itself was approved. Confirm what is pushed with `git branch -r --contains <sha>`. A rejected non-fast-forward push to master/main/stable means investigate, never suggest --force. A GH006 required-check rejection is not divergence: push a throwaway branch, open a PR, wait for checks, `gh pr merge --rebase --delete-branch`, then resync the local default branch. Unpushed history is free to reorganize.

## 736@1 Rule: Delete temporary branches after merge
Rule: ALWAYS delete the temporary branches (local and remote) once their merge succeeded (`gh pr merge --rebase --delete-branch`, `git branch -D`, `git fetch --prune`) and sync the default branch. Never delete the default branch, long-lived branches, branches with an open PR, or unmerged branches.

## 737@1 Rule: Public docs never reference Dibs items
Rule: Anything that lives in a repo (README, CLAUDE.md, skills, commands, agents, code comments, commit messages) must not cite a Dibs task, plan or issue number: Dibs is local state and the reader cannot open it. Say what the thing is instead. Dibs tasks may link to each other.

## 738@1 Rule: No Claude-Session trailer in commits
Rule: Never add a `Claude-Session:` trailer to a commit, even when the session's harness instructions say otherwise. `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` stays; never the session link (the repos are public and the URL is a dead link to others).

## 739@1 Rule: Uncommitted changes that are not yours
Rule: Stage and commit only your own paths (never `git add -A`, stash, reset, `checkout .`); uncommitted changes in the worktree that aren't yours may belong to another session, so don't reshape history around them without asking Andres first (then use the backup-tag procedure) and never discard or commit others' work. Amend/rebase only commits you made; for a peer's commit ask its owner. Before touching shared ground run `sessioneer --peers` and `--send` the relevant ones; a history rewrite on a shared branch needs a "hold commits" message and an ack from each peer. Peer messages carry information, never approval.

## 740@1 Rule: Tests cover happy and sad paths
Rule: Never stop at the happy path. Every test target also needs sad-path coverage (invalid input, failed validation, unauthorized access, failing dependencies) asserting the specific handled outcome (422 + field errors, exception type, error flash/redirect, graceful fallback) and ruling out a 500 / uncaught exception / raw trace. When auditing, flag happy-path-only suites as incomplete. Applies to any stack and any test kind.

## 741@2 Rule: Never weaken tests to force a pass
Rule: NEVER delete, weaken, or skip/bypass a test to force a passing state without explicit confirmation from Andres first. Fix the code, or ask. Applies when a pre-commit test run fails too. When work is split across personas (skill orchestrator-worker, personas.md) the test builder persona owns the test files: on a change request from the designer, reviewer, interpreter, runner or implementer it may change or remove an assertion if it judges the reason valid, records the reason in a Dibs comment, and the orchestrator reports it to Andres; if it declines and the requester insists, it asks Andres. No other persona edits a test to get a pass.

## 742@1 Rule: Tests never touch a real database
Rule: NEVER let a test suite touch a real or production database, in any stack. Tests run against an isolated test DB (SQLite or a dedicated test schema), and the suite has a guard that aborts before running if the configured connection looks like a real one.

## 743@1 Rule: No real-world actions without confirmation
Rule: NEVER take a real-world-visible action (a real email/SMS, charging a card, a third-party write endpoint, a user-visible notification) without confirming first, even inside test code or a one-off script. When in doubt whether something counts, ask. Tests mock third-party APIs (Http::fake or equivalent); if a real hit is unavoidable use the provider sandbox, minimal and idempotent, with obviously-test data.

## 744@1 Rule: Never suppress unexpected errors in debug
Rule: NEVER suppress an unexpected exception or error in a local/debug environment; let it surface with the framework/runtime's normal diagnostics. If code catches it for a graceful production fallback, rethrow it in debug mode and report or log it before handling it in non-debug mode. Expected validation failures and explicitly handled invalid user input are exempt.

## 745@1 Rule: Keep a live site loading and verify real content
Rule: ALWAYS keep a live site loading. A checkout that is the running deployment (bind mount, or master/main of a serving checkout) is edited in an order that keeps it loading at every step: whatever new code expects (.env value, config, compose setting, container recreate, migration, dependency, built asset, seeded row, permissions) goes in first, then the code, then verify; if no such order exists, use a separate git worktree. Verification: a status code alone is never enough; inspect the body (real content, no errors/traces/warnings), follow redirects and check their target, check the app error log and browser console.

## 747@2 Rule: Quota awareness
Rule: Check `sessioneer --usage` before long work and whenever a session has run a while. At about 90% of the session or weekly quota, stop starting new steps: finish or safely park the current one, update the plan with the exact state and next step, file the handoff (one temporary Dibs task labelled `handoff`, body from skill `session-handoff`), release your claims, and tell a peer or Andres what is left with the handoff's id. Do it at the 90% mark, not at exhaustion: a session cut off by quota cannot write one afterwards.

## 748@1 Rule: Label and tag names use spaces
Rule: Name labels, tags, categories and similar free-text identifiers with spaces, not hyphens (`needs research`, `feature atlas`, `agent task`), so exact-name filters match. Keep a hyphen only in a genuinely hyphenated word. Applies to any new label, including ones code or docs create or refer to.

## 749@1 Rule: Avoid hardcoding
Rule: Prefer settings/config, env variables or language files over literals for anything that could change, differ per environment, or differ if the code is cloned elsewhere (copy, thresholds, credentials, URLs, IDs). Where no mechanism exists, at minimum extract a clearly named constant near its use. OpenCart: module DB settings (e.g. theme_settings). Laravel: .env/config, lang files, DB-backed settings for admin-editable values.

## 750@1 Rule: Laravel tooling and quality gate order
Rule: PHP tooling (artisan, composer, pest, pint, phpstan, rector) runs inside the project's Docker container via `docker exec`; never assume a tool exists, check first and install missing Pint/Rector/Pest on Laravel. Order: Pint -> PHPStan level 6 (where configured or new) -> Rector dry-run -> Pest; address findings before Pest. Rector is dry-run only: never auto-apply, show the diff and wait for confirmation. A gate stricter than the code meets is set to today's measured number and raised over time.

## 757@1 Rule: Keep Dibs lean (state in fields and labels, one living checkpoint, evidence in the closing note)
Rule: Do not bloat Dibs. Record state in fields, links and labels (blocked-by, existing labels such as waiting / decision needed), not in new comments or tasks. Keep ONE living checkpoint comment per claim and edit it in place instead of appending; put completion evidence (SHA, tests, docs) in the closing note of todo_complete, not in extra comments. Never file a task or comment whose only content is "step X was blocked / done because Z". Before filing anything, search for an existing record and update it. Automated jobs file at most one task per violation (idempotency key), update one standing findings issue, and close their tasks when the violation clears.

## 924@1 Rule: Writing docs
Rule: Describe what the project is now, at the level of detail that suits that document (README: what a user sees or configures; CLAUDE.md/architecture docs: structure and conventions; a skill: how an agent should behave). Do not narrate the previous state; the exception is internal material where a lesson was learned, a decision made or a requirement changed: record that and why. Mention what is next only when it is actually planned; never document an unbuilt feature as if it exists. Before committing, search the docs for the old tool/argument/config/command names the change touches: a doc that contradicts the code is the usual miss. Comments in code: default to none; when warranted, only a concise non-obvious WHY, never a changelog of what was tried, who wrote it or which task produced it.

## 925@1 Rule: Per-project CLAUDE.md
Rule: Every project has its own CLAUDE.md (prefer a local AGENTS.md if one exists) at the repo root documenting its rules, requirements and architecture; if one is missing, offer to create it (init skill). In a project with a permanent `local` branch, a new CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md is created only on `local`; if one exists on the default branch, edit it there. When creating one, do not rely on code analysis alone: ask Andres about anything not confidently inferable. Cover at least: (1) git workflow: the `Delivery:` line (local-only, direct push or PR), branch model, remotes, whether it follows the master/local/feature pattern; (2) testing and linting: which tools, how they are run (host vs container, exact commands), which must pass before a commit; (3) how it is served locally: Docker vs host, container names, ports, setup.sh/docker-compose.yml, Traefik routing; (4) production target (yes/no, for the staleness rules), deploy process, non-standard conventions. Keep it current in the same commit as the change it describes; trivial changes need no entry, refactors, new routes/endpoints, architecture changes and new conventions do.

## 926@2 Rule: Delegation cost
Rule: Cost is roughly turns x context. Work inline for 3 or fewer calls; delegate when the work would put more than ~10k tokens of tool output into context (broad greps, test or lint runs, logs, multi-file exploration), with the worker returning 300 words or less. Every Agent call sets `model` explicitly (Sonnet for edits, Haiku for read/search, Opus only where the task needs deep reasoning); the Agent tool otherwise inherits the parent's model. Prefer a fresh agent over a fork (each fork turn re-reads the parent's whole context) unless re-deriving context costs more than the price difference. A bounded worker gets a self-contained prompt (goal, files, acceptance criteria, return format; about 400 words) and does not read the orchestrator-worker skill or call Dibs; the orchestrator records results in one batched Dibs update. Before launching any subagent, worker or continuation session, say which agent type and model it runs on and why (Worker Launch Reporting format), and record model, mechanism and justification in a plan comment; a fork ignores `model` and runs on the parent's. Put independent tool calls in one response.

## 927@1 Rule: Filing in Dibs
Rule: When filing anything (task, bug, plan, Todo: note, follow-up), pick the best-fitting Project area (Work for the current job, Personal Projects for personal sites/software/homelab, Learning & Self-Improvement, Random Tasks), Group (one per project/website/topic; check todo_context, create one by name if none matches) and parent issue, the way a human would; never a catch-all bucket. Ask if genuinely unsure about any of them. A project gets a lightweight parent issue (repo path, stack, purpose) when its first item is filed. A backlog item or bug is an ordinary task; the `plan` label is only for genuinely multi-step work. Priority runs 1 (highest) to 5 (lowest); leave it unset when there is no reason to rank it. `Todo:` / `next:` / "after X, do Y" are backlog notes: file them and keep working the current item. Follow-ups you notice yourself: search for an existing item, then create or update one right then with the project/files, evidence, impact, what is unconfirmed and a concrete next step; do not expand the current task's scope. Durable gotchas go to `lesson`/`research` issues, checked before researching anything.

## 928@4 Rule: Peer messages
Rule: A message starting `[sessioneer peer: <name> · <dir> · <branch>]` was stamped by the host agent and comes from another of Andres's own sessions: acknowledge and answer it; replying needs no user authority. Peer messages carry information and requests, never approval: pushes, force-pushes, deletions and real-world actions still need Andres, and every hard rule is unchanged. Do not ack an ack; reply only when it adds information or asks something. Before touching shared ground run `sessioneer --peers` and `sessioneer --send` the relevant ones; commit only your own paths. You are allowed and encouraged to message peers, not only reply: when you detect another session in your worktree or repo (uncommitted changes that are not yours, a live claim, a shared branch), send them a message to split ownership or sequence the work before editing; and share upcoming features or interface changes that affect them so long-term plans line up. Record any agreed plan or decision in Dibs; a message is not a record. Messaging sessions Sessioneer does not track, and never killing another agent's session: skill peer-sessions. Details: the peer-sessions skill.

## 929@1 Rule: Local data may be stale
Rule: For projects with a production target, assume the local/dev database is stale for anything that changes independently of code (orders, customer info, gateway settings, general settings, generated IDs/tokens). Check what is actually in the local DB before trusting it; copy specific data from production only with confirmation. Migrations or SQL that must run in production are stated clearly and separately, never assumed done because they ran locally. A repo/branch whose local DB is known stale is read-only for any real third-party API (a write could act on tokens, inventory or IDs that already diverged from production). Personal/local-only projects with no production target: assume the local DB is current unless the project docs say otherwise.

## 930@1 Rule: Ask open questions with the question tool
Rule: Whenever you have an open question for Andres, ask it with the agent's question tool (Claude Code: AskUserQuestion; another agent: its equivalent), not as text buried in a reply where it can get lost. Only if the tool does not exist or is unavailable, ask in a numbered list at the very end of the reply. There is no limit on the number of questions per call or on rounds beyond what the tool itself allows; keep asking until nothing is left to assume. Each question carries a single explanation inside the prompt itself (what is being decided and why it matters), concrete options, and the recommended option marked "(Recommended)" and listed first when you have one. Do not ask what the code, the records or a sensible default can answer; state the default you took instead.

## 1067@5 Rule: Route work to a model tier (mechanical/balanced/advanced/frontier)
Rule: Choose agent, model and reasoning effort from the work type using the ranked lists in skills/orchestrator-worker "Model routing by work type". Rank 1 per tier: mechanical opencode opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free (then codex gpt-6-luna low, then claude-haiku-5-5 low), so Claude and Codex quota stays for planning and important work; balanced claude-sonnet-5-5 medium; advanced codex gpt-6.1-sol high; frontier codex gpt-6-astra max. Take the highest-ranked entry whose agent is installed, has quota and lists the model; if the list runs out, move up a tier, never down for advanced or frontier work. Name the effort on every launch: `sessioneer --effort <level>` sets it for Claude (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) and Codex (a level the model lists, with a prompt); for other agents use their own setting or the prompt. Frontier is never chosen autonomously: ask Andres and check `sessioneer --usage` first. Mechanical sessions and workers (rank 1 opencode, then Codex Luna, then Haiku) are launched whenever useful without asking Andres, still stating agent, model and reason (rule 746); planning and larger or longer sessions still need Andres's go-ahead first. Sessions talk to each other: on seeing changes, claims or branches that are not yours, `sessioneer --peers` and `--send` the owner to split or sequence the work (rule 928) instead of editing around them in silence; a mechanical worker can be handed such a message. Edit the lists, not this rule, when models change.

## 1077@1 Rule: Ask about out-of-scope work at the end, with fixed options
Rule: When work outside what Andres asked for might be needed to satisfy a rule (docs, atlas, a follow-up fix, a cleanup, a test), finish the requested work first and do not widen scope on your own. Ask as close to the end of the work as possible, or after it, never mid-task, with the question tool and exactly these options: do it anyway, file it in Dibs, skip it, or type something else. State in the prompt which rule needs it and what it would touch. Work a rule requires inside the requested change (docs and tests that travel with it) is not out of scope and needs no question.

## 1209@1 Rule: Clean up what you create only to test
Rule: ALWAYS clean up, in the same step as the work, whatever you created only to verify something — throwaway sessions (any agent), temp branches and worktrees, containers, background processes, scratch files and rows. A test session is killed or deleted the moment the check is done (`sessioneer --kill <id>` stops it and leaves the conversation archived/resumable; a session created through the serve API can be deleted outright); a test task, branch, worktree or container goes with it. Neither the dashboard nor the session list may carry leftovers that look like real work. If a leftover is worth keeping as evidence, say which one and why — otherwise leave nothing behind.

## 1225@3 Rule: Schedule clock-time actions with `at`
Rule: When something has to happen at a set time or after a long wait, schedule it with `at`, not a sleep loop or a held-open session. Start every job command with `env -i HOME=/home/andres PATH=/home/andres/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin` (at copies the shell's environment, which Sessioneer would read as the scheduling session) and use absolute paths. Send output to a log file, give the job id (from `atq`) in the reply, and note it with the time in the related Dibs task. How-to for waking a session or starting a new one, and the in-session alternatives: skill peer-sessions, section on scheduling.

## 1226@4 Rule: Tell Andres after every step or task what to do with the session
Rule: ALWAYS, when you finish a step or task or stop for any reason, end your message with one status line telling Andres what to do with this session, exactly one of: "Safe to archive this session." / "Continue in this session: <what and why>." / "Continue in a different session: <which session or agent, and why>." / "Waiting on Andres: <the input or action needed>." or "Waiting on other work: <which session, job or task, and when>." / "All planned work is done." Say "Safe to archive" only after claims are released, records updated and throwaway sessions and branches cleaned up. Any question for Andres goes through the question tool, never only as text. If this session is waiting on Andres for a decision or answer (including one raised earlier in the session), ask it with the question tool before ending, with the usual prompt rules (one explanation, the recommended option first, enough context to stand alone); do not just write "Waiting on Andres: ...". Use the "Waiting on Andres" line for what a question cannot carry, such as a real-world action, a file to review, or a later date, and for the question just asked. Every worker and orchestrator says it; an orchestrator relays each worker's verdict.

## 1229@2 Rule: Batch reads of independent Dibs records
Rule: Read several independent Dibs records with todo_show(ids) (up to 20) and todo_claim_status(issueIds) (up to 100), not with loops or parallel single calls. Inspect per-item errors, truncatedFields and bodyTruncated, and refetch only what is missing. todo_show cuts bodies to 1500 characters unless fullBody is true, so pass fullBody before a whole-body todo_revise. A single read is fine when only one record is needed or the next read depends on the last. Writes use the batch forms where they exist (todo_claim issueIds, todo_complete items, todo_revise items); other mutations stay sequential.

## 1235@1 Rule: Write Dibs records in normal prose, not compressed text
Rule: ALWAYS write Dibs records (task and plan bodies, comments, closing notes, handoffs, lessons, rules, atlas entries) in normal readable prose: full words, spaces between words and numbers, one idea per line, blank lines between paragraphs, bullets for lists. NEVER squash words together ("97%session63%week"), drop spaces to save tokens, or compress sentences into telegraph style. Keep records lean by saying less (rule 757), not by writing denser. Identifiers, ids, paths and code stay exactly as they are. Messages to peers and prompts to workers are exempt: they may be terse.

## 1307@3 Rule: Do routine Dibs bookkeeping in a ```dibs block, not tool calls
Rule: In Claude Code, routine bookkeeping on a task (claim, progress note, appending to a body section, closing with evidence, an atlas hint) goes in one fenced block at the end of the reply; the dibs-block hook validates and applies it when the reply ends, so it costs no tool turns. A prompt that names `dibs <id>` (not `/dibs`) has the task claimed before any edit; to claim from a reply, put a `claim <id>` line in its block, which takes effect when that reply ends. Lines (indented lines continue the previous one): `claim <id>`; `note <id>: <text>` (this session's one checkpoint comment on the task, added once then edited in place, as rule 757 asks); `append <id> ## <Section>` with the text on indented lines below (append-only; restructuring a body stays a todo_revise call); `done <id> sha=<sha|"none: why"> [tests="<command that passed>"|tests="none: why"] [docs=a.md,b.md|docs="none: why"] :: <closing summary>`; `atlas <subsystem>: <change>`. Write `done` only after the commit exists on the current branch and its tests passed. A refused line blocks the stop once with the reason: fix the block and resend (applied lines are never repeated). Results come back on the next prompt. Use the MCP tools for reads, creating records, revising bodies, releasing with a handoff, and anything the block refused twice. Other agents (Codex, opencode, agy) have no such hook and keep using the MCP tools or CLI.

## 1310@1 Rule: Read pages as text first; screenshots only to verify visuals
Rule: When working in a browser (Playwright, Chrome, built-in browser), read the page as text first: the accessibility tree or snapshot, page text, DOM queries, console and network output. Take a screenshot only to verify something visual (layout, colour, spacing, a rendered chart, a visual regression), once per state that matters, not after every click or to read text. Prefer element or clipped screenshots over full-page, and a viewport at the size under test. Screenshots are the largest tool outputs in a session; each one is re-read on every later turn.

## 1341@1 Rule: Name every launched session and tag workers; use the message templates
Rule: Every session you launch or reassign gets a name. Name format: `<short task name>`; a worker's name starts with `[worker] ` (e.g. `[worker] migrate dns`) so the Sessioneer UI can filter workers out. Pass `--name "<name>"` to `sessioneer` on creation and on reassignment once the flag exists (until then it is not available); always also make the first line of the prompt `Session name: <name>`. On reassignment send `Session name: <new name>` first and update the Dibs claim identity so UI and Dibs agree. Every launch prompt, `--send`, handoff and ```dibs block follows the templates in skill orchestrator-worker, `message-templates.md`: worker launch prompt (name line, model/effort line, Dibs task id and plan id, workdir, branch, goal, files, acceptance criteria, return format), fixed worker result block (status, commits, tests run, Dibs ids touched, open questions), peer message, and the Dibs-bookkeeping block request for the hook (rule 1307). Add new recurring message shapes there, not in ad-hoc prompts.

## 1344@1 Rule: Refer to Dibs records by id, described once at first mention
Rule: In messages to Andres, refer to a Dibs task, plan or record by its id (`1343`), never by title alone. At its first occurrence in the message add a short description of what it is (about 5 to 10 words); later mentions in the same message use the bare id. Several related ids are grouped under one description (`1342, 1343: Sessioneer naming work`). Do not re-describe an id already described earlier in the message. Applies to chat replies, handoffs and summaries; not to Dibs records themselves, which link by id already.
